subject: End-to-end latency gap analysis and next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jmiller@acme.com>
Cc: contracts_acme@acme.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: End-to-end latency gap analysis and next steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can move toward a POC: 

1) Targets you gave: p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 420ms (end-to-end, user device -> Acme backend -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> response). Please confirm if p99 420ms is strict or flexible by +/- 50ms.

2) Current provider numbers (you mentioned these were sampled across peak window): we requested the CSV of the 7-day tail distribution — please attach when convenient.

3) Streaming requirements: you indicated partial streaming for multi-turn chat (token streaming to UX). Concurrency: typical steady-state 600 active sessions, burst to 2.4k. Average tokens per turn ~ 18; peak turn tokens ~ 120.

4) Throughput profile: baseline 20 RPS sustained (1k QPS tokens across traffic shaping), peak 80 RPS for 45s bursts.

Action items we agreed: 
- You to share the export of current-provider tail stats (CSV).
- Redwood to produce a short-fitment matrix comparing hosted p95/p99 under your traffic profile + recommended concurrency/streaming knobs (I attached a first-draft SLO matrix).
- Quick lab POC schedule: propose Wed/Thu next week for an isolated perf run (we'll need a 2-hour window).

I've attached: redwood-hosted-slo-matrix.pdf (draft) and flagged the items we need to validate.

If any of the numbers above are off, correct me in reply and we'll update the fitment doc.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
O: 415-555-0123 | evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-hosted-slo-matrix.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
From: Jordan Miller <jmiller@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts_acme@acme.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 17:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: End-to-end latency gap analysis and next steps

Evelyn — thanks for the concise recap. Couple of clarifications: 

- p99 of 420ms is our current internal SLO for the UI team; the product team treats anything below 500ms as acceptable for now, but the business would prefer to be below 450ms for the checkout flow. So the 420ms is a hard target for the checkout path, flexible (+30ms) for other flows.

- I'll attach the 7-day export (CSV) from our provider — contains per-request timing, region, and error flags. Note: we only sampled traffic from us-west.

- On streaming: checkout flow is non-streaming (single response), support chat and recommendation flows use streaming. We'll send an expected distribution per flow in a follow-up.

Proposed POC window: Thu May 6, 10–12 PDT. Please confirm Redwood can reserve capacity and provide the runbook and expected test tools you want us to execute.

Best,
Jordan Miller
Senior Eng Manager, Platform
Acme Commerce
Attachment: acme-current-provider-stats.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

Jordan / Evelyn — small follow-up from my side with high-level test plan and what we need to validate for p95/p99: 

Test plan (short):
- Run isolated fixture in us-west with a single model variant (gpt-medium-quantized) to compare per-token times vs your CSV. We'll reproduce request path including simulated Acme backend processing (20ms added latency) to get end-to-end numbers.
- Two traffic shapes: steady-state 20 RPS and a 45s burst up to 80 RPS; include concurrency knobs for streaming sessions to match 600 steady / 2.4k burst.
- Measure: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, tail error rates, first-byte latency (for streaming), and sustained throughput.

We can reserve a Dedicated test bucket for May 6, 10–12 PDT. I'll attach the runbook after Evelyn confirms. Can Acme provide the post-processed CSV mapping of request->flow type (checkout vs chat vs recs)? That will help isolate the checkout path p99.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: (runbook to follow)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jmiller@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: End-to-end latency gap analysis and next steps

Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the CSV. Short synth of next steps and owners before the POC: 

1) Acme (Jordan) — drop per-flow labels on the provided CSV and confirm the checkout-only sample that should be treated as 'hard p99 target'. Deadline: Mon May 3 EOD.

2) Redwood (Ben) — finalize and circulate the POC runbook (incl. seed data, simulated Acme backend hook, exact load profiles). Deadline: Mon May 3 EOD.

3) Redwood (Marcus) — provision dedicated test capacity and share the reservation + rollback policy. Deadline: Tue May 4 EOD.

4) Evelyn — coordinate internal legal for a short POC addendum for limited logs retention during the test. Deadline: Tue May 4 EOD.

POC execution: Thu May 6, 10–12 PDT as proposed. Expected deliverables after run: a CSV with per-request timings, p50/p95/p99 numbers, and a short slide that maps gaps to configuration knobs (batching, KV cache, streaming concurrency).

If anything needs to shift, call it out and we'll move the reservation. Looking forward to validating whether our hosted stack can hit the checkout p99 420ms with the stated traffic model.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
